claims.statement: Zendesk documents an OAuth refresh token returned with the access token in the authorization code flow and exchanged at /oauth/tokens (grant_type refresh_token) for a new access token and refresh token; the old refresh token stops working immediately, and the default lifetime is 30 days (configurable from 7 to 90 days). The client credentials flow returns no refresh token.

sources.supports: Refresh token: Used behind the scenes to get a new access token when the current one expires. ... Refresh token 30 days by default, configurable from 7 to 90 days ... The old refresh token stops working right away.
Unlike the authorization code flow, no user redirect is required and Zendesk does not return a refresh token.

openQuestions.question: The pages show example refresh tokens of differing shapes (32 and 64 characters) and state no format; no shape is recorded.
This candidate is recorded from the claims above only; format, variants, history and benign siblings have not been researched.
